I should pull up the ticket and property details before acting. There's a prior open ticket about a stiff lock from 9/22, which points to a landlord wear-and-tear issue, and the landlord's notes say emergencies can be approved without asking first.

This is a night lockout, so it's a P1 escalation — I'll assign Hackney Locks 24/7, note the likely landlord cost responsibility pending the locksmith's report, and keep in mind the £250 spend limit (though this qualifies as an emergency regardless). I'll make sure the tenant knows the locksmith is on the way now, that he isn't being told to pay anything yet since cost depends on the report, and that the prior ticket supports a lock-fault explanation. I'll reach him by SMS since he's on the phone, plus follow up by email per his preference, and I'll create a new emergency ticket linked to R-4766 rather than trying to change the severity of the existing one.

arguments.body: Hi Jonah, sorry about tonight. We've sent Hackney Locks 24/7 (our out-of-hours locksmith) to 27 Bethnal Green Road, target arrival tonight between 9.30 and 11.30pm; we'll confirm if that changes. Please don't pay them anything tonight. Your lock was reported stiff on 22 Sep, so this may well be a lock fault, which is the landlord's cost; the locksmith's report will settle who pays and nobody will ask you for money before we've spoken to you. If you can, wait somewhere warm nearby, and please don't force the door. The spare-key route (office, Mon-Fri 9-17.30, £50 refundable deposit) is there too, but isn't needed if the locksmith gets you in. If you feel unsafe or unwell, call 999. We'll email you tomorrow with an update.

Dear Margaret, tonight (Sat 10 Oct) your tenant Jonah Okafor was locked out of 27 Bethnal Green Road when his key snapped in the front door lock. He had reported it stiff on 22 Sep (R-4766, not yet actioned - our apologies). Under your emergency instruction we've sent Hackney Locks 24/7 to extract the key, restore entry and secure the door; this is within your emergency authority. The locksmith will report on cause. If the lock has failed it is your cost and we'll bring any lock replacement quote to you; we won't charge the tenant unless the report shows misuse. We'll update you tomorrow.
